questiontext.text:
The table below shows marks obtained by eight students in a mathematics and physics exam. Calculate the Spearman’s coefficient of rank correlation.

Note: Give your answers correct to \(2\) decimal places.

Mathematics \({@x1@}\) \({@x2@}\) \({@x3@}\) \({@x4@}\) \({@x5@}\) \({@x6@}\) \({@x7@}\) \({@x8@}\)
Physics \({@y1@}\) \({@y2@}\) \({@y3@}\) \({@y4@}\) \({@y5@}\) \({@y6@}\) \({@y7@}\) \({@y8@}\)

a. Spearman’s coefficient of rank correlation \(\rho=\) [[input:ans1]]. [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

b. Examine the calculated Spearman’s coefficient of rank correlation \((\rho )\) for the given data in mathematics and physics. How would you interpret this correlation coefficient in the context of the marks obtained by the eight students?

[[input:ans2]].[[validation:ans2]][[feedback:prt2]]

\(\displaystyle \sum d^{2}={@total_d_squared@}\)

\(n=\) no. of ranks \(=8\)

Spearman rank correlation coefficient \(\displaystyle r=1- \frac{ 6\sum d^2}{n(n^2-1)}\)

\( \displaystyle r=1- \frac{6({@total_d_squared@})}{8(64-1)}\)

\( r=1-\frac{{@6*total_d_squared@}}{504}=1-{@(6*total_d_squared)/504@}\)

\(={@ta_1@}\)
